NO. 065 · Coast & Tidal Flats / Threskiornithidae · Ibises & Spoonbills

Eurasian Spoonbill

白琵鹭 · bái pí lù Platalea leucorodia
Winter visitor Rare 70–95 cm Protected (Class II) IUCN LC

The white-faced cousin, with a yellow tip to the bill

Almost identical to the Black-faced Spoonbill, with just two differences: the face is white rather than black, and the end of the bill is yellow rather than wholly black. It is not a regular, but every winter one or two turn up among the spoonbills.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • BillLong and flattened, expanded into a spoon at the tip, blackish-grey overall but clearly yellow at the tip — the key difference from Black-faced Spoonbill.
  • FaceBare facial skin pale yellow to flesh, not black; yellow bare skin around the eye and on the throat.
  • PlumageWhite throughout; in breeding condition a pale yellow wash at the base of the neck and on the breast, with loose yellow plumes.
  • LegsBlack and fairly long, made for wading in shallow water.

Behaviour

It feeds exactly as the Black-faced Spoonbill does, sweeping the spoon-shaped bill through the water and taking fish and prawns by touch. It mixes with Black-faced Spoonbills and egrets, but in far smaller numbers. A scarce winter visitor in South China, with occasional Delta records on mudflats and at fish ponds.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qi'ao Island tidal flats
  • Jinwan coastal fish ponds
  • Hengqin wetlands
Field note
A nationally protected species (Class II). Check a spoonbill flock bird by bird: black face and black bill means Black-faced (Class I); white face and a yellow bill tip means Eurasian (Class II).
